newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Peace troops in standoff with Serb police chief.
newsitem.headline: Peace troops in standoff with Serb police chief.

text.p: NATO troops fired warning shots in the air during a tense stand-off with a notorious Serb police chief in northwest Bosnia, a NATO spokesman said on Tuesday.

The spokesman said the incident took place on Monday after a patrol of Czech troops in the alliance-led peace force tried to confiscate an unauthorised weapon belonging to the police chief of Prijedor, Simo Drljaca.
Major Brett Boudreau told reporters the troops spotted an MP-5 machine-pistol on the back shelf of Drljaca's car and ordered him to hand it over.
Later, Drljaca was surrounded by the troops outside the vehicle who fired two warning shots in the air.
"The police chief then fired one shot in the air," Boudreau said.

The IFOR (Implementation Force) troops withdrew when they in turn were surrounded by at least 10 of Drljaca's own men, some of whom were also armed with weapons, such as AK47s, not allowed under the Dayton peace agreement.
After talks with the U.N.'s international police task force, an investigation into the incident was launched which Boudreau said could have "potentially serious consequences".
Boudreau declined to specify what action could be taken by NATO, but said the issue had also been raised with Bosnian Serb Interior Minister Dragan Kijac.
Thousands of Moslems were killed in the Prijedor area, which was also the scene of the some of worst ethnic cleansings and other atrocities, at the start of Bosnia's war in 1992.
On Saturday, Drljaca threatened not to open a road to allow Moslems to return to their former home districts to vote in the country's election despite an agreement between all parties.
In the event, the road was opened but few Moslems took advantage of the facility.
